prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1342; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: The policyholder reported being rear-ended while stopped at a light. Both vehicles were drivable, so no tow was needed.
Entry 2: The claimant contacted us without a lawyer and described neck and back pain as severe, asking how to start a medical payments request.
Entry 3: The other driver gave the same account of the rear impact that the policyholder did, and the witness statements line up with both.
Entry 4: Photos of both vehicles show damage that is mostly in line with the impact described. A few old scratches may predate this crash, so I have noted them separately.
Entry 5: The police report confirms the claimant was riding in the vehicle at the time of the collision.
Entry 6: The claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far, with the same sequence of events and no changes in the details.
Entry 7: Treatment records show a usual course of care that tapered off as the patient improved. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from prior claims or medical history.
Entry 8: The severity of the claimed injury does not fit the very light impact shown in the photos and reports. I have flagged this gap for supervisor review.
Entry 9: Policy history shows nothing suggesting the damage happened before coverage began. The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
Entry 10: Liability appears clear based on the evidence collected. The injury portion stays open pending further medical review and the flagged inconsistency.
